描述_EN: ‘meiping’ vases were made at many different chinese kilns from the 12th century to the 19th. when salting bought this piece it was already more than 400 years old. its decoration, which is drawn in black under a turquoise glaze, was influenced by ceramics from syria. although they were used to hold prunus flowers, they served other functions as well. this vase is one of a pair. the appearance of these hitherto unknown objects on the british art market inspired artists to create new forms and patterns. vases of this shape are called ‘meiping’ in chinese, meaning 'prunus vase'. this elegant vase appealed to george salting (1835-1909), a passionate collector who bequeathed to the museum a large number of chinese ceramics. the chinese had always treasured ancient ceramics, but it was only after the opening up of china to the west after 1840 that antique items became available to other collectors.
描述_ZN: '梅瓶'从12世纪到19世纪在许多不同的中国窑场被制造。 当Salting买下这件作品时，它已经有400多年的历史了。 其装饰是在绿松石的釉面下用黑色绘制的，受到了叙利亚陶瓷的影响。 虽然它们是用来盛放梅花的，但它们也有其他功能。 这个花瓶是一对中的一个。 这些迄今未知的物品在英国艺术市场上的出现激发了艺术家们创造新的形式和图案。 这种形状的花瓶在中国被称为 "梅花瓶"，意思是 "梅花瓶"。 这种优雅的花瓶吸引了George Salting（1835-1909），一位热情的收藏家，他将大量的中国瓷器遗赠给了博物馆。 中国人一直珍视古代陶瓷，但只是在1840年中国向西方开放后，其他收藏家才有机会获得古董。
